research_question: How do repetition, context cues and automaticity contribute to habit formation, and what limits apply to popular claims about habit timelines?

sources.title: How Are Habits Formed: Modelling Habit Formation in the Real World
sources.publisher: European Journal of Social Psychology / Wiley
notes: A 12-week study followed 96 volunteers repeating a chosen daily behaviour in the same context.
Automaticity generally increased over time but varied across behaviours and participants.
The results do not support a universal timeline for every habit.

sources.title: The Automatic Component of Habit in Health Behavior: Habit as Cue-Contingent Automaticity
sources.reliability: High: peer-reviewed article indexed in PubMed
notes: Three studies investigated cues and automaticity in health-related habits.
The research treats habits as learned cue-response relationships, not just high frequency.
A specified situational cue helped increase automaticity in a flossing behaviour.

sources.title: Psychology of Habit
sources.reliability: High: peer-reviewed review in Annual Review of Psychology
notes: The review describes cognitive, motivational and neurobiological aspects of habits.
Habits and goal-directed decision-making can guide actions together.
Repeated responses in recurring contexts are central to habit development.

sources.title: Expert Meeting on Healthy Habits: Habit Formation and Habit Change
sources.reliability: High: U.S. federal research institute meeting resource
notes: The expert meeting considered affect, reinforcement learning, motivation, memory, goals and context.
Habit formation and habit change are multidimensional, rather than explained by a single motivational formula.

sources.title: The Automatic Component of Habit in Health Behavior
sources.reliability: High: university research repository hosting peer-reviewed article metadata
notes: The repository confirms bibliographic information for Orbell and Verplanken's 2010 study.
The study frames habit as cue-contingent automaticity and reports three demonstrations of cue importance.
